name: Persona-based Walkthroughs
description:
A persona walkthrough examines a proposed design by stepping through an activity from the perspective represented by a persona. At each stage, designers consider the persona's goals, circumstances, capabilities and likely questions.

The method can help teams expose mismatches between a concept and previously identified user needs, provided that the persona itself is grounded in credible research.
whenToUse: Use persona walkthroughs when evaluating early flows, scenarios or concepts and when research-based personas already exist.
steps: Define the task or scenario to examine.
Establish the persona's relevant goals and context.
Move through the design one step at a time.
At each point, ask what the persona knows, expects and needs.
Record barriers, uncertainties and unsupported assumptions.
Repeat with personas representing meaningfully different circumstances.
Use the findings to revise the design or identify questions for user research.
lookOutFor: A walkthrough does not turn a fictional representation into an actual participant.
Weak or stereotypical personas will produce weak walkthroughs.
Do not use persona walkthroughs as a substitute for accessibility evaluation or research with relevant users.

resources.citation: Cooper, A. (1999). *The Inmates Are Running the Asylum*. Sams.
Pruitt, J. & Adlin, T. (2006). *The Persona Lifecycle*. Morgan Kaufmann.
